四级核心词汇 · 07英文原文

The Second Price on the Receipt

小票上的第二个价格 · 595 词 · 9 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1A young merchant called Tavi sold cloth at an indoor market. She hoped domestic commerce would offer more stability than her former occupation. Sales increased during a holiday boom, yet her savings shrank. She compared her retail receipts with her bank account. A corporation handled each transaction and transferred the money every quarter. She marked a second price beside each purchase to emphasize the difference. That figure was what she received after the platform deducted its fees.

2The manager blamed inflation and international shipping. He pointed to a currency index and a recent increase in the price of cotton. Neither explained the second figure. An accountant found a difference in the contract. Tavi's initial plan offered a discount to any new merchant. After three months the incentive expired. The platform began to charge for storage and distribution in addition to its commission.

3Tavi faced a dilemma. A loan could cover her assistant's wage, but she might go bankrupt if her revenue continued to decline. A consultant proposed an investment in direct sales. Tavi asked him to estimate the volume they would need. He contrasted gross earnings with delivery costs. The margin was so small that a single extra trip could wipe out the benefit.

4The merchants suggested a cooperative. They could consolidate deliveries and distribute stock from one place. A rival offered a vacant room with low rent and utilities. Before they made a joint deposit, Tavi asked how much each seller could supply. A small enterprise could not guarantee regular stock. They needed flexible orders to cope with shortages and a reserve to meet an unexpected increase in demand.

5The corporation's executive wanted an exclusive agreement despite the recent trouble. He offered a prominent position in its catalog and a commercial label with its trademark. Tavi inquired about the additional charges. One applied if a package exceeded a specified weight. A second applied when a buyer canceled an order after dispatch. The executive agreed to delete the latter clause for a trial. Tavi refused the exclusivity and asked for a written amendment.

6The cooperative obtained credit to purchase a shared cart. It issued one receipt. Consumers could see what they paid for a commodity and what they paid for delivery. The new arrangement brought a modest profit. The trend held. It kept the balance positive and let Tavi retain her assistant. She offered him a bonus for designing the order sheet.

7One buyer asked for an alternative to delivery. She needed a predictable pickup time and was willing to pay a few cents more for it. Tavi set a lower rate for a regular pickup and a higher one for a rush order. The change let her accumulate savings and repay some debt. Besides, it did not restrict where her assistant could work.

8A local institution offered to sponsor a warehouse extension. Tavi wanted to expand only after they had assessed the risk. The latest figures showed that orders could fluctuate by twenty percent in a week. Extra storage could become a costly burden. The cooperative set a definite limit on how much it would spend, and kept its original room.

9A prospective entrepreneur asked Tavi how to choose a platform. She showed him the old receipt. It appeared to prove that a sale was complete, but one line depended on terms she had overlooked. She circled both prices and drew a third box for the actual delivery cost. He copied the three figures. Tavi had gone to a financial adviser hoping for a rescue. She left with a way to see trouble sooner.

四级核心词汇 · 07中文译文

小票上的第二个价格

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1年轻商贩塔薇在室内市场卖布。她希望在国内做生意比原来的工作更稳定。节日期间生意兴旺，销售额涨了，存款却少了。她拿零售小票和银行账户核对。每笔交易由一家公司经手，每季度再把钱转给她。她在每笔购买旁标出第二个金额，特意把差别标清。这个数字是平台扣完费用后她真正收到的钱。

2市场经理把原因归到通货膨胀和国际运输上，还指给她看汇率指数和棉花最近的涨价。两样都解释不了第二个数字。会计找到了合同里的不同。塔薇最初选的方案给新商家折扣，三个月后优惠就到期了。此后平台除了抽佣，还开始收仓储和配送费。

3塔薇左右为难。她可以借钱付助手的工资，可收入再往下掉，她自己就可能破产。一位顾问提议投入一点钱试做直销。塔薇请他估算，要有多少单生意才能撑住。顾问把毛收入和配送成本放在一起比。利润空间太小，多跑一趟就可能把收益全花掉。

4商贩们建议成立合作社，把配送合在一起，从同一个地方发货。一位竞争对手愿意提供空房，房租和水电费都低。大家合交押金前，塔薇先问每家能供多少货。小商户无法保证一直有存货，所以订单要灵活，也要留一点储备，才能应对断货或突然多起来的需求。

5尽管前面出了问题，平台高管还是想签独家协议，愿意给商家一个醒目的目录位置，再提供带自家商标的商业标签。塔薇追问额外费用。包裹超重会加一项，顾客在货发出后取消订单又会加一项。高管同意试行一段时间，暂时删掉后一条。塔薇谢绝了独家安排，请他把修改写进合同。

6合作社用信贷买了一辆公用推车，统一开一张小票。顾客能看清商品多少钱、配送又多少钱。新办法带来了一点利润，后来也一直维持着。账面保持盈余，塔薇也留住了助手。她给助手一笔奖金，感谢他设计订货单。

7一位顾客问，能否改成自己来取。她希望取货时间能提前确定，愿意为此多付几分钱。塔薇把普通自提的费率定得低一些，加急单则收得高一些。这样一来，她又攒下一些钱，还掉部分债务。助手也能继续选择自己在哪儿工作。

8当地一家机构愿意出资扩建仓库。塔薇想先评估风险，再决定是否扩大。最新数字显示，订单量一周之内就可能上下波动两成。多租的仓储可能变成一笔沉重开支。合作社给这项花费定了明确上限，最后仍用原来的那间房。

9一位打算创业的人问塔薇该怎么挑销售平台。塔薇给他看旧小票。它看起来证明一笔买卖已经结清，其实还有一行取决于她先前漏看的条款。她圈起两个金额，又画了第三个方框，填进实际配送成本。对方把三个数字都抄了下来。当初塔薇去找财务顾问，是希望有人帮她渡过难关。她带回来的，则是一种能更早看见难关的办法。
